## P0 — Trust the current build (6/12)

| # | Work order | Phase | Area | Priority | Depends | Effort | Risk | Status | Notes |

| AX-001 | Fix the two 16 KB ASan/LSan leaks | P0 | Runtime | P0 | — | M | med | `[x]` | All three leak sites closed (c840f9a). The audit's attribution to `archx_fn___archx_user_main` was wrong; the real defect was in the collection pipeline: (1) comprehension growth (cap==len so the last push reallocated), (2) the min/max generator temp claimed without being freed, (3) the for-each loop variable re-cloned over the previous binding. ASan now 11/11 CLEAN; ci/leakcheck.c is an independent gate that provably fails on a leak. |
| AX-002 | Make integer overflow actually trap on every path | P0 | Codegen | P0 | — | M | high | `[~]` | Trapping i64 via llvm.s*.with.overflow + checked const folding (e55ea1d), and this round closed the last two silent-wrap paths: `abs(i64::MIN)` used to print a NEGATIVE number (negation is now the checked intrinsic, so it traps) and `2 ** 63` used to print i64::MIN (integer `**` used a plain unchecked `mul`; both multiplies are now checked, gated on whether the value is actually used, so `2 ** 40`, `2 ** 62`, `(-2) ** 63` and `1 ** 100` still answer correctly while `2 ** 63`, `(2 ** 40) ** 2` and `3 ** 40` trap). tests/cli.rs::overflowing_integer_operations_trap_instead_of_wrapping asserts six trapping cases and four representable ones. REMAINING: the explicit `wrapping_*` intrinsics for the native dialect (an API for opting out where the program means modular arithmetic) — not started, so AX-002 stays partial. |
| AX-003 | Reconcile versions, docs, and numbers | P0 | Docs | P0 | — | S | low | `[x]` | Version single-sourced: Cargo.toml 0.9.0 -> 0.9.1 (the CLI already read CARGO_PKG_VERSION; `archx --version` now prints 0.9.1) and benchmarks/run.sh now derives every version string from Cargo.toml instead of hard-coding 0.9.0. The README benchmark table is GENERATED from ci/out/benchmarks.txt by tools/sync_readme_benchmarks.py, which also rewrites the two perf claims; `--check` fails on drift and was verified to fail on an injected stale number. tools/check_test_count.py asserts the quoted count equals the `#[test]` attributes (79 = 41 unit + 38 CLI; the old 68 was stale). ## Verified baseline

Re-measure after every work order.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo build --release` | clean, 13 pre-existing warnings (AX-004 target) |
| `cargo test --release` | 42 unit + 38 CLI = **80 pass, 0 fail** |
| CI run 45999706770 | **all 4 jobs green** (Linux, macOS, Windows, records) |
| ASan+LSan `ci/logs/asan_lsan.log` | **11/11 CLEAN** |
| Leak gate `ci/logs/leakcheck.log` | **12/12 clean** (Linux only — see note) |
| `benchmarks/pipelines.archx.lang` vs CPython 3.12 | byte-identical `5333140919445` |
| Audit baseline (94 Python probes) | 73/94 = 78 % |

**Leak-coverage note.** Both leak checks are Linux-only: ASan does not link against
Archx IR on this toolchain, and `--wrap` needs GNU ld/lld (macOS `ld64` rejects it;
Windows MSVC ignores it and fails with LNK1120). "Zero leaks" is a Linux result;
macOS and Windows are covered for correctness by the full suite, not for leak-freedom.
